AddItemSchema.description: `POST /cart/items`. One is the default because that is what a product page sends.
AddItemSchema.title: AddItemSchema

AddressCreateSchema.description:
A new address. `label`, `line2`, `region` and `phone` are optional, as the model has them.

The lengths are the model's, repeated here so an over-long field is a `400` naming the field
rather than a database error on PostgreSQL and a silent pass on SQLite — the difference `M1.2`
found the hard way. The required fields also carry a floor of one character: the model declares
them non-blank, and nothing in the database refuses `recipient = ""`, so without this an address
checkout could not use would be stored happily.
AddressCreateSchema.title: AddressCreateSchema

AddressSchema.description: A stored address, as a client sees it (`API.md` section 8).
AddressSchema.title: AddressSchema

AddressUpdateSchema.description: Every field optional: a `PATCH` sends only what changed (`API.md` section 8).
AddressUpdateSchema.title: AddressUpdateSchema

CartLineSchema.description:
One line, priced from the variant as it stands now (`DATA-MODEL.md` section 2).

`available_stock` is here so the quantity stepper can cap itself at the same number the API
enforces, instead of discovering the limit by being refused.
CartLineSchema.title: CartLineSchema

CartSchema.description:
The whole cart.

`id` is null when the account has no cart yet, which is a normal state rather than an error:
reading a cart never creates one, so an empty payload is what a shopper who has added nothing
gets.
CartSchema.title: CartSchema

CategoryRefSchema.description: Just enough category to label a card or a breadcrumb.
CategoryRefSchema.title: CategoryRefSchema

CreditListSchema.description:
The attribution list.

Not paginated: `US-6.1` asks for every shipped image, and the catalog ships 46 of them.
CreditListSchema.title: CreditListSchema

CreditSchema.description:
Attribution for one source image (`US-6.1`, `ADR-0012`).

Mirrors the `ImageCredit` row rather than reshaping it: `US-6.1` names creator, licence and
source URL, and `ADR-0012` records the source title and the provider alongside them.
CreditSchema.title: CreditSchema

MockPaymentRequestSchema.description:
Both mock endpoints act on an order's open payment.

The order is named by its human-facing `number`, the same value the confirmation shows, rather
than by a payment id: the caller is holding an order, and asking it to keep a payment id as well
would be asking it to remember something the API can look up.
MockPaymentRequestSchema.title: MockPaymentRequestSchema

MockPaymentResultSchema.description:
What the mock answers: the attempt, and where the order ended up.

The order's status is repeated because it is the outcome the client acts on — `paid` moves the
shopper to the confirmation, `cancelled` back to the cart — and reading it from the payment alone
would make the client infer the order's state from a payment's.
MockPaymentResultSchema.title: MockPaymentResultSchema

OrderCreateSchema.description:
`POST /orders`.

The same two ways to give an address as the quote (`US-4.1`), plus the shipping method chosen
from the options the quote returned. `email` is optional because the account already has one: a
signed-in shopper is contacted at their address unless they say otherwise.
OrderCreateSchema.title: OrderCreateSchema

OrderDetailSchema.description:
`GET /orders/{number}`: the order, plus the timeline of how it reached its status.

Extends `OrderSchema` rather than restating it, so the detail page cannot render an order that
differs from the one the confirmation showed: creation and this route answer with the same fields,
and only this one adds to them.
OrderDetailSchema.title: OrderDetailSchema

OrderEventSchema.description:
One step of an order's status timeline (`API.md` section 6, `US-4.6`).

No `actor`. The customer-facing timeline answers *what* happened and *when*; who did it is the
operator console's question (`US-5.5`, `M5`), and sending an operator's identity to a customer
would be a disclosure this page has no use for.
OrderEventSchema.title: OrderEventSchema

OrderItemSchema.description: A line as the receipt shows it — the snapshot, never a live `ProductVariant`.
OrderItemSchema.title: OrderItemSchema

OrderPageSchema.description: A page of the history, in the envelope every listing here answers with (`API.md` section 4).
OrderPageSchema.title: OrderPageSchema

OrderSchema.description: A placed order. Shared by creation now, and the history and detail pages at `M4.6`.
OrderSchema.title: OrderSchema

OrderShippingAddressSchema.description: Where the order went, as it was at the time. Contrast `AddressSchema`, which is the book.
OrderShippingAddressSchema.title: OrderShippingAddressSchema

OrderSummarySchema.description:
One row of the order history (`US-4.5`).

Deliberately not `OrderSchema`: a row is a number, a date, a status and a total. Naming the lines
and the address for every order on the page would be the whole receipt, twenty-four times over, to
render four fields — the same reason `catalog.schemas` keeps its listing and its detail payloads
apart.
OrderSummarySchema.title: OrderSummarySchema

PageFilters.description: Paging parameters, shared by the paginated routes.
PageFilters.title: PageFilters

PaymentSchema.description: One attempt, as a client sees it. Never anything card-shaped, because none is stored.
PaymentSchema.title: PaymentSchema

ProductCardSchema.description: A listing row. No variants: the grid does not render them.
ProductCardSchema.title: ProductCardSchema

ProductFilters.description:
Query parameters for `GET /products` (`API.md` section 4).

`min_price` and `max_price` are integer cents, matching the payload convention in `API.md`
section 1, so a client never converts to a decimal in order to filter.

allOf.description:
`sort` values from `API.md` section 4. The `-` prefix means descending.

Members are upper case because `Enum` already defines `name` and `value`; a member named
`name` would shadow one of them.
allOf.title: SortOption

ProductFilters.title: ProductFilters

ProfileUpdateSchema.description: `US-2.4`. An absent field means "leave it unchanged", because a `PATCH` sends only changes.
ProfileUpdateSchema.title: ProfileUpdateSchema

QuoteAddressSchema.description:
A delivery address supplied inline — `US-4.1`'s "enter a new one".

The constraints mirror `accounts.schemas.AddressCreateSchema`, the address book this could be
saved into, with the address-book-only fields (`label`, `is_default`) left out: a checkout does
not name an address or make one the default.
QuoteAddressSchema.title: QuoteAddressSchema

QuoteRequestSchema.description:
`POST /checkout/quote`.

Exactly one of `address_id` (a saved address) or `address` (a new one) — `US-4.1`'s two ways to
give an address. The "exactly one" rule is checked in the endpoint rather than here so the
refusal is a plain `400` with a readable message, not a model-level pydantic error whose field
location is the whole body.
QuoteRequestSchema.title: QuoteRequestSchema

QuoteSchema.description:
The quote: the cart's subtotal, and every shipping option with the total it produces.

The address is not echoed back. It is a precondition the request had to satisfy, not a result,
and what a checkout needs to render from this is money.
QuoteSchema.title: QuoteSchema

SetQuantitySchema.description:
`PATCH /cart/items/{line_id}`.

Zero is deliberately not a value: removing a line is `US-3.3`'s endpoint, and a stored zero
would be a line every total has to remember to skip.
SetQuantitySchema.title: SetQuantitySchema

ShippingOptionSchema.description: One shipping method and what choosing it does to the total.
ShippingOptionSchema.title: ShippingOptionSchema

SortOption.description:
`sort` values from `API.md` section 4. The `-` prefix means descending.

Members are upper case because `Enum` already defines `name` and `value`; a member named
`name` would shadow one of them.
SortOption.title: SortOption

TokenSchema.description:
The sign-in payload.

The refresh token is deliberately absent. `ADR-0009` delivers it only as an httpOnly cookie so
that no script — including a compromised one — can read it, and `API.md` section 2 documents the
access token as the only token in the body.
TokenSchema.title: TokenSchema

UserSchema.description: The account as a client sees it. Never the password, never a token.
UserSchema.title: UserSchema

post.description:
The first address becomes the default whether or not the client asked for it.

An account whose only address is not the default is a state checkout would have to special-case
for no benefit, so it is not reachable.

delete.description:
`US-2.5`.

Deleting the default promotes the oldest survivor, so the account keeps exactly one default for
as long as it has any address at all — the same invariant the other endpoints hold.

patch.description: `US-2.5`. Only the fields present in the body are touched.

post.description:
`US-2.2`.

One message for every failure, so the endpoint cannot be used to find out which addresses have
accounts. Django runs the password hasher even for an unknown address, so the timing does not
give it away either.
`US-2.3`. Ends the session server-side; the access token is short-lived and expires anyway.

patch.description:
`US-2.4`: change the display name.

An absent field means "leave it", not "clear it" — the difference between editing a name and
erasing one. There is a single editable field today; the schema is written so it stays correct
if that stops being true.

post.description:
`US-2.3`: silent refresh. The token is read from the cookie, never from the body.

The origin check runs before the cookie is read, so a cross-site request cannot spend a token —
and cannot revoke one either, which is the sharper edge: replaying a stale cookie through a
forged request would trip reuse detection and sign the real customer out.

get.description: `US-3.4`. An account with no cart gets an empty payload, and asking creates nothing.

post.description:
`US-3.1`.

Adding a variant that is already on the cart adds to its quantity rather than starting a second
line, which is what the uniqueness in `DATA-MODEL.md` section 2 means and what the cap below
then applies to the total.

delete.description:
`US-3.3`. The cart survives with its remaining lines, and the response is the cart so the
client can re-render the totals it just changed.

patch.description:
`US-3.2`. Above stock is refused rather than quietly capped: the client asked for a number and
is told it cannot have it, which is the `409` in `API.md` section 5.

get.description: Every category, nested under its parent. Not paginated: a tree is small and shaped.
One category plus its products, paginated. An unknown slug is a `404`.

post.description:
`US-4.1` and `US-4.2`: the subtotal, and every shipping option with its total.

`total_cents = subtotal_cents + shipping_cents` is the same arithmetic the order's own check
constraint holds, so a total shown here is a total `M4.3` can carry onto the receipt.

get.description:
Attribution for every image the catalog ships (`US-6.1`).

Read through the images rather than through the credit table, because the criterion asks for
every *shipped* image: `ProductImage.credit` is nullable with `on_delete=SET_NULL`, so a credit
row can outlive the image that described it. Going through the forward foreign key rather than
the reverse accessor follows `ADR-0014`.

Not paginated: `US-6.1` asks for the complete list, and 46 attribution lines belong on one page.

`US-4.5`: the caller's own orders, newest first.

Scoped by `user`, and that scope *is* the authorisation — there is no "every order" route, so an
order belonging to somebody else is not filtered out here, it was never in the set.

`item_count` is annotated rather than summed in Python: one query for the page instead of one per
row, and it is the number the row's "2 items" shows.

post.description:
`US-4.4`: turn the cart into an order, reserving its stock and starting a payment.

`201` when this request made the order, `200` when an `Idempotency-Key` it had already seen
answered from the row that key produced — the same body either way, so a client retrying a submit
whose answer it never saw can take the first response as final.

`409` for the states of the *cart* that checkout cannot sell: empty, holding something no longer
for sale, or holding more of a variant than is left. Each reads as the cart's problem rather than
the request's, which is why none is a `400`.

get.description:
`US-4.6`: one order — its lines, where it went, its totals, and how it reached its status.

A `404` for an order that is not the caller's rather than a `403`. The number is unguessable
(`generate_order_number`), and a refusal that distinguished "yours but missing" from "somebody
else's" would confirm that the second one exists — the reasoning `accounts/addresses_api.py` gives
for an address.

The timeline is read in the order `M4.1` wrote it (`OrderEvent.Meta.ordering`, chronological), so
the page shows the events in the sequence they happened rather than the reverse.

post.description:
`US-4.3`: capture the order's payment and move the order to match.

The capture decides the order's fate, not the caller: `capture` answers with the attempt's status
and that status picks the transition. A real adapter that *declined* — answering `False` rather
than raising — would therefore cancel the order exactly as the mock's fail endpoint does, with no
branch here to remember to update.

The failure path, on request (`ADR-0010`) — QA drives a decline instead of hoping for one.

The order is cancelled, which returns its reserved stock (`orders/services.py`): a reservation
made at order creation is released when the order is, or the shop would sell stock it had already
set aside for a purchase that never happened.

get.description:
Filtered, sorted, paginated products.

An unknown `category` filters to nothing rather than erroring, so the storefront can render its
explicit no-results state (`US-1.3`).

allOf.description:
`sort` values from `API.md` section 4. The `-` prefix means descending.

Members are upper case because `Enum` already defines `name` and `value`; a member named
`name` would shadow one of them.
allOf.title: SortOption

get.description: One product with its gallery and variants nested, for the detail page (`US-1.2`).
